norms.text: Fish dry on the landing racks.
The mud walls are replastered every year.

taboos.text: Building in stone on the landing bank.

values.text: The ford, which was worked before the well was dug.

contempts.text: Being told to haul stone for a well whose water the landing does not drink.

people.text: The station folk count everything twice and drink from a cracked well.

trade.text: The raft is the only way a cart crosses. Carts pay by the wheel.

addressTerms.text: By name among themselves; traveller to strangers.

neverSaid.text: That the landing could not last without the station's trade.

grievances.text: The station wants stone hauled across the ford for its own well.

views.text: Good customers; poor judges of water.
